content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Connecting to PostgreSQL and MySQL helps you reason about driver and client requirements. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Driver and client requirements. Then connect it to Connection configuration. The remaining syllabus points—Handling database-specific types, Connection errors and timeouts—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Connecting to PostgreSQL and MySQL
content_blocks.code:
require "sqlite3"
db = SQLite3::Database.new(":memory:")
db.execute("CREATE TABLE tasks (id INTEGER, title TEXT)")
db.execute("INSERT INTO tasks VALUES (?, ?)", [1, "Learn Ruby"])
puts db.get_first_value("SELECT title FROM tasks WHERE id = ?", 1)
db.close
